rule: Fable/the coordinator must never do plan-implementation work itself (implement/repair/probe/judge) — only coordinate, fan work to cheap agents, and require adversarial+concurring cross-vendor review before trusting any fix.

The coordinator may relay a genuinely cross-vendor review onto GitHub and land on it autonomously, but only when the reviewing vendor actually differs from the authoring vendor and the trust gate reflects a real dispatched review, not a laundered self-approval.

On detecting a crash-looping process, stop it (and its recreating supervisor) without asking permission, but first check co-tenancy/shared-volume impact and gather diagnostics, escalating only if stopping would take down another tenant's production workload.

Treat any provider safety/cyber-filter refusal of authorized defensive security work as a tool failure to record and route around (different vendor), never as evidence the task itself was wrong, and note any silent model-tier reroute caused by the classifier.

Every session that starts test Docker containers/volumes on the shared host must remove them (docker rm -f -v) on all exit paths and must never run a global docker system/volume prune on the shared host.
check: PreToolUse-hook regex-blocking literal `docker system prune`/`docker volume prune -f` Bash invocations; supplementable with a CI-job/post-test check comparing pre/post `docker ps`/`docker volume ls -f dangling=true` counts against a leak threshold
misses: per-container/per-volume deletion loops that sum to the same effect, obfuscated or split prune commands, leaks from crashed sessions that never reach an exit-path cleanup step, and any host other than the one instrumented

rule: The active experiment coordinator may restart/reboot experiment infrastructure (up to full VM reboots) without asking, but only after verifying no other session holds in-flight work on the target, recording rollback state, and excluding known production-serving/stateful hosts.
check: PreToolUse-hook maintaining a denylist of protected hostnames (e.g. precision's embed host, hermes) that blocks restart/reboot commands targeting them regardless of stated authorization
misses: the actual lease/in-flight-work verification (requires live log/process introspection, not a static list), the 'only active session' premise, and any newly-added production host not yet in the denylist

rule: All GitHub traffic (reads and writes) must default to the App token via plain `gh`/`git`; use `env -u GH_TOKEN` only for administrative actions or when the founder wants his own name on it, and never fall back silently to OAuth when the ambient token is unset.
check: a session-start or wrapper-script check of `$GH_TOKEN` (non-empty) before the first `gh`/`git` call, exporting/prefixing from `gh-app-token claude` if empty; or a post-call check on `gh api rate_limit`'s `limit` field (5000 vs 7300) flagging wrong identity
misses: whether a given action actually qualifies as 'administrative' (requires judgment), and background-job sessions where the check itself is never invoked because bashrc sourcing is skipped — the documented recurring failure mode

rule: Any session that hits GitHub rate limiting (403/429, secondary-limit Retry-After, or near-zero x-ratelimit-remaining) must alert the founder explicitly and track it as a limiting factor rather than silently backing off.
check: PostToolUse-hook scanning `gh`/`git` command output for 403/429/rate-limit indicators and firing a notification
misses: rate-limit signals in commands that don't surface headers by default (most gh calls without -i), gradual throttling that never returns an explicit error, and the qualitative requirement to 'track as a limiting factor' in reporting

rule: Adversarial hardening must continue, unbounded, until a full attack round returns clean, and a reported-clean round must be verified via artifacts (real tool calls, genuine failed probes against the current code) rather than trusted on the lane's own summary.

Before adding any new standing rule, skill, persona, routing entry, or hook to the harness, run the leverage-vs-prior gate (decay/maintenance-dependence/what-vs-how tests) and prefer deletion over addition.

Never design a guard/hook so that it blocks an action even when the founder is directly and explicitly authorizing it live in the conversation; guards must gate on staleness/indirection of authorization, not on live direct authorization itself, and the deleted merge-bypass-guard.sh must not be reinstalled.

The protected-path-write-guard's token-path false positive on reads may be worked around with a script-file wrapper, but that workaround is scoped strictly to read false positives and must never be used to defeat a true-positive write block.
Any authored config referencing another service (routing, origins, tunnels, proxies) must use hostnames/service DNS, never raw IP addresses, except where a system physically requires one.
check: CI-job/lint-rule regex-scanning config files (Traefik/cloudflared/k8s manifests etc.) for literal IPv4 addresses in host/origin/upstream fields
misses: legitimate cases where an IP is physically required (the rule's own carve-out, which the scanner can't distinguish without an allowlist), IPs embedded via templating/variables rather than literals, and pre-existing legacy IP config that is flagged as drift rather than a hard violation
